title: Relative separatedness descends along universally closed surjections of spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $B,U,V$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:U\to B$, $q:V\to B$ and $a:U\to V$ satisfy $q\circ a=p$. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces use the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose $|a|$ is surjective and $a$ is universally closed: for every algebraic space $V^{\prime}\to V$, the map $|U\times_VV^{\prime}|\to|V^{\prime}|$ is closed. If $p$ is separated, then $q$ is separated. Here separated means that the relative diagonal into the fibre square over $B$ is a representable closed immersion, that is, its every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. No separatedness of $B$ over $S$, finite-type, quasi-compactness, Noetherian, or flatness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Put $A=U\times_BU$, $C=V\times_BV$ and $F=a\times_Ba:A\to C$. Factor $F$ as $U\times_BU\to U\times_BV\to V\times_BV$; these are base changes of $a$ on the second and first coordinates. Each further base change is closed by universal closedness of $a$. A composite of closed maps is closed, since it sends a closed set successively to two closed sets. Thus $F$ is universally closed. Comparing the two projections of the sheaf fibre products gives $F\Delta_p=\Delta_q a$.

source.place: Tag 05Z2 (lemma-image-universally-closed-separated), first diagram and its factorization of the right vertical map.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed] applied to $p:U\to B$, its diagonal $\Delta_p$ is universally closed. The composition argument of step 1 now shows that $h=F\Delta_p:U\to C$ is universally closed. This criterion allows an arbitrary algebraic-space target $B$, with no separatedness assumption on $B\to S$.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, separated case: universal closedness of the map from the test pullback of X; Tag 04Y0 (lemma-separated-diagonal-proper).

proof.text: For any algebraic space $T\to C$, put $R=T\times_CU$ using $h$, and $Q=T\times_CV$ using $\Delta_q$. The equality in step 1 identifies $R$ with $Q\times_VU$: on sections the mutually inverse maps send $(t,u)$ to $((t,a(u)),u)$ and forget the repeated $a(u)$. Write $b:R\to Q$ and $d:Q\to T$. The point-fibre-product assertion of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] makes $|b|$ surjective because $|a|$ is surjective, and the same node makes $|b|$ continuous. For any closed $E\subseteq|Q|$, its inverse image under $|b|$ is closed; its image under the closed map $|R|\to|T|$ is therefore closed. Surjectivity gives $|d|(E)=|R\to T|(|b|^{-1}E)$. Hence $d$ is closed for every algebraic-space test $T$, proving that $\Delta_q$ is universally closed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed] to $q:V\to B$. Universal closedness of $\Delta_q$, proved in step 3, makes $q$ separated, that is, its relative diagonal is a representable closed immersion.
